clue.text: Pig called out for flavouring

parts.note: Peppa Pig is the cartoon pig of children's television

explanation.surface: A farmer shouting to a pig about seasoning, or naming a pig after a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: Peppa Pig is a hugely popular British children's cartoon character; her name, said out loud, is the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground peppercorns are among the commonest seasonings added to food for taste.

clue.text: Morose at first, and cut up, faced with ordeal at school

parts.note: the opening letter of Morose

explanation.surface: A gloomy, wounded pupil facing a dreaded test.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed cut comes first in the grid, sitting on top of M.
explanation.definitionFit: A school test is a nerve-racking trial that pupils must sit through and endure.

clue.text: Dragged in to fix something, being clued-up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lead pushed into a socket, or a stopper jammed into a hole
second meaning: well informed and in touch with what is going on

explanation.surface: Someone roped in to mend things because they know their stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, connected by a plug; figuratively, informal slang for being well informed and up to date.

clue.text: Absence of emotion in 'About a Boy'

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A critic noting that the Nick Hornby novel About a Boy is coldly unemotional.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make About a Boy look like a title; the three words are simply strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational thought is traditionally set against feeling, so cool logic is thinking without passion.

clue.text: Acknowledge regularly ignored age-old expression of relief

parts.note: to thank someone is to acknowledge them

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means every other letter is dropped and the rest kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of age-old

explanation.surface: An ancient sigh of relief that people regularly fail to recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: People exclaim it when a danger has passed or a worry has been lifted.

clue.text: Film in which maidens with auto hell-bent!

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film plot summary: two women in a car, recklessly determined.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair summary of the 1991 road movie, in which two women flee across America by car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Ridley Scott's 1991 road movie starring Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis.

clue.text: 'In a while': translation of note giving French farewell

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a bit is a short while

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A translator rendering a note that says 'in a while' as a French goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged note goes inside A BIT. The surface pretends the French phrase is the translation, which it nearly is.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means see you soon, a parting greeting used when leaving someone.

clue.text: Loudly demand massage

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: a need is a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: A client noisily insisting on a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Masseurs work muscles with pressing, squeezing hand movements, as a baker works dough.

clue.text: Describing the Speaker's wild coital roar

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of the Speaker of the House making a lusty noise in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S suggests the Speaker of the House of Commons; here it is any public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, and the adjective relates to rhetoric and grand public delivery.

clue.text: With no end in sight, planet consumed in flood

indicators.note: when the end cannot be seen, the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: the ringed sixth planet from the sun
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An endless deluge in which a whole planet is swallowed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something until it can hold no more liquid is to drench or inundate it.

clue.text: I see Europe limit what's threatened by global warming

parts.note: taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like see
E is the abbreviation for Europe
a cap is a limit, as on spending

explanation.surface: Someone noticing that Europe is capping emissions to fight climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: I see sounds like the first word of the answer, which is a tempting shortcut, but the pieces build it letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice sheets are melting as temperatures rise, a key worry of climate science.

clue.text: Person trapped in grand lavatory departs with contrary mood and unpleasant atmosphere

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
loo is British slang for a lavatory
a man is a person

something trapped in something else is enclosed by it

parts.note: taken as written
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a posh toilet leaves in a foul temper, souring the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The person goes inside the run of grand, lavatory and departs; then mood is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a pervasive pessimism or despondency hanging over a situation.

clue.text: Quick to take in a bit of old cash in sale of old clothes

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: fleet of foot means quick
taken as written
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Hurrying to grab some old coins at a jumble sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of stalls selling second-hand goods, notably cheap used garments.

clue.text: Made smooth moves, fluttering lids

indicators.note: fluttering things move about restlessly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flirt making a pass while batting their eyelids.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide is to move smoothly across a surface without friction, past tense here.

clue.text: A nameless visionary with a pleasant odour

indicators.note: nameless means without the abbreviation for name, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a romantic is an idealistic dreamer

explanation.surface: An anonymous dreamer who happens to smell nice.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant herbs and spices give off a pleasing, spicy scent, so smelling sweet fits.

clue.text: Save for one time cricket won't be played

definitions.text: Save for one time cricket won't be played

parts.note: surface reading: except for, as if listing exceptions to a playing schedule

parts.words: one time cricket won't be played
parts.note: setter's reading: put money aside for a wet occasion, as in the proverb, since rain stops cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket fixture list with one exception noted.
explanation.walkthrough: Save for looks like except for; it is the verb of the saying about putting money by for hard times. Cricket stops when it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keeping reserves against future hardship, pictured as a wet day spoiling plans.

clue.text: According to Spooner, conducted a terrible piece of campaigning

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: conducted is ran and terrible is bad: ran a bad, with the opening sounds swapped

explanation.surface: A political campaign that was badly run.
explanation.definitionFit: An online advertisement strip across a web page is a common tool of marketing and political campaigns.

clue.text: Surprising appearance of genetic material (lacking nitrogen) startled Darwin

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named element is taken out

parts.note: DNA carries genetic information
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, here removed

indicators.note: something startled jumps about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Darwin startled by a surprising discovery about genetics.
explanation.walkthrough: A dawn raid is a police swoop at first light, or a surprise early share purchase in the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Police or investors swoop unexpectedly at first light, so it is an unannounced arrival.

clue.text: Far off and regularly war-weary

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of war-weary

explanation.surface: A soldier who is distant and constantly tired of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a distance is remote, not here, in a separate place.

clue.text: Black Magic assortment is something avoided by dieters

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed selection, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Black Magic, a British boxed chocolate assortment, is shunned by people watching their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Magic is a classic British box of assorted chocolates, which makes assortment look like part of the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: McDonald's double-decker burger is high in calories, so slimmers steer clear of it.

clue.text: Expert with 'original' notion: spending time to get seasonal ingredients

indicators.note: original means novel and inventive, so the letters are freshly arranged

parts.note: a sage is a wise expert
and means with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever cook with a novel idea who takes time over festive cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage and onion is the classic British stuffing for the Christmas turkey, hence seasonal.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb and vegetable make the traditional festive stuffing, a pun on seasoning too.

clue.text: Run outside

definitions.note: the prefix extra- means outside, as in extramural
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Latin-derived prefix for beyond or outside

explanation.walkthrough: Run outside reads like an instruction; in cricket a bye or wide counts as one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket scores include byes and wides credited to the batting side, and the Latin prefix means beyond.

clue.text: Extremely pious holy man over here

parts.note: the outer letters of pious

explanation.surface: A very devout saint beckoning someone across.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered sound is used to attract someone's attention discreetly, like saying come here.

clue.text: 'Little sister,' princess admitted, 'is smooth mover'

parts.note: SR is the short form of sister
Kate, the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A little girl explaining that her sister, playing princess, glides gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on ice or roller skates glides along gracefully.

clue.text: Everyman's introducing two ways to be revealing

MODE and ST (street), two words for a way

clue.text: In her seat, the rider initially will do this!

definitions.text: In her seat, the rider initially will do this!

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a rider's seat on a horse is a saddle

clue.text: 'Shy old Lawrence' is actually kind of a wolf

O is the abbreviation for old
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A revelation that the bashful Lawrence was really a wolf in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence is the soldier and writer known as Lawrence of Arabia.
